problem: The number of computers affected by the spread of some ransomware after $t$ days can be modeled by the function $f(t)=\frac{100\,({t}^{3}+2)}{t+1}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change in the number of infected computers when $t=9$ days?

feedback.problem: The temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, of a rapidly cooling substance after $t$ minutes can be modeled by the function $F(t)=250-{t}^{3}.$ Find the instantaneous rate at which the temperature of the substance is changing with respect to time at the moment when the temperature of the substance is equal to $34$ degrees Fahrenheit.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the temperature of the substance is $34$ degrees Fahrenheit, the time can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}34 & =250-{t}^{3} \\ {t}^{3} & =216 \\ t & =6\end{aligned}
$$

The instantaneous rate at which the temperature of the substance is changing when $t=6$ minutes is equal to ${F}^{′}(6).$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $F(t)$ with respect to $t$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(250-{t}^{3})=-3{t}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $t=6$ gives

$$
{F}^{′}(6)=-3(6)^{2}=-108.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the temperature of the substance is changing when $t=6$ minutes is $-108$ degrees Fahrenheit per minute.
